title: Linear Equations in Two Variables
prerequisites: Ability to solve a linear equation in one variable.
Familiarity with the Cartesian plane and plotting points.
Understanding of substitution into an algebraic expression.
Knowledge of the terms coefficient and constant.

topics.title: Linear Equations and Their Solutions
topics.quick_summary: An equation of the form ax + by + c = 0 with a and b not both zero is linear in two variables, and it has infinitely many solutions.
topics.real_life: If two pens and three pencils cost ₹50, there are many possible price combinations — a single equation in two unknowns can never pin down both.

detailed.definition: A linear equation in two variables is an equation of the form ax + by + c = 0, where a, b and c are real numbers and a and b are not both zero. A solution is an ordered pair (x, y) that satisfies the equation.
detailed.key_idea: One equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions because each chosen value of x determines a value of y. Only a second independent equation can fix a unique pair.
detailed.working_principle: To find solutions, substitute any convenient value for one variable and solve for the other. Choosing x = 0 and y = 0 gives the two intercepts, which are usually the easiest points to plot.
applications: The graph of a linear equation in two variables is always a straight line.
Every point on the line is a solution, and every solution lies on the line.
y = mx is a line through the origin; x = a is vertical and y = b is horizontal.

points: Standard form: ax + by + c = 0, with a and b not both zero.
A linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions.
Its graph is always a straight line; two points are enough to draw it.
x = a is a line parallel to the y-axis; y = b is parallel to the x-axis.
An equation in one variable represents a point on the number line but a line in the plane.
mistakes: Saying a linear equation in two variables has only one solution.
Plotting only one point and trying to draw the line through it.
Confusing x = 3 (a vertical line in the plane) with the single point 3 on the number line.
topics.memory_hook: 'One equation, two unknowns, infinitely many answers — and all of them lie on one line.'
topics.advanced: The line is the set of all solutions, so solving simultaneous equations is geometrically the intersection of two lines. Parallel lines mean no solution and coincident lines mean infinitely many — algebra and geometry saying the same thing.
